turns.t: Sorry, sorry, I'm late. The train sat outside the station for twenty minutes and I have to be somewhere by eleven. Can we go quickly?
Of course. Come in, sit down, catch your breath. Where would you like to start?
My heart, really. It's been fluttering, like it skips and then races, mostly in the evenings when I finally sit down.
Tell me more about that.
Well, like I said, it flutters. Sometimes it's a few seconds, sometimes it goes on for a minute or so, and it happens a few evenings a week.
Mm-hm.
It doesn't stop me doing anything. It just feels odd, and I notice it more than I'd like to.
I see. And when did you first notice it?
Ooh. Um. It could have been last month, or the month before that, I honestly couldn't tell you. It sort of crept up on me.
That's perfectly all right. I can see in your notes that you take carbimazole. What dose are you on at the moment?
Twenty... maybe 20 mg? It was changed at some point, I think, or I think it was. The box is in my other bag, sorry.
Don't apologise. How often do you take it?
Once a day, in the morning with breakfast. That's the one thing I never forget, because the alarm on my phone goes off.
Good. Has anything else changed in the last few weeks, anything at all, that you can think of?
Not really. Honestly, I'd just like to know if I need a bigger dose or a smaller one and then get on with my day.
I understand, but I wouldn't want to change a dose by guesswork. The blood result will tell me far more than the box in your bag could.
So you can't just put it up today and see?
I could, but if your levels are already low that could make you feel worse. Let me keep that thought for a moment.
Fine. It's just that I've done this dance before and it takes forever.
I hear you. Before I decide anything, are you allergic to any medicines, now or in the past?
Penicillin. I came out in hives when I was about six, my mum always reminds me, and I've avoided it ever since.
That's important, thank you. I'll make sure it's flagged. Any other medicine or food that's ever given you trouble?
No, just that one. That's the whole list, I promise.
Okay. Tell me what the fluttering is like when it happens. Do you feel faint, or does it just feel like a noise in your chest?
More like a noise. Like a little bird trapped behind my ribs. It gets my attention and then it goes away on its own.
No, I'm just thinking. Palpitations like that are very common when thyroid hormone levels are still settling on treatment.
So it's the tablets not working properly?
Not necessarily. It can take a few months for the dose to find the right level, and then it can overshoot or undershoot a little. It happens to lots of people.
Please don't give up the tablets. I'd rather you called me first. What I think is most likely is the thyroid hormone level not being fully settled yet.
And that's it? That's all you think it is?
It's my best working guess, based on what you've told me. I'd like to repeat your thyroid blood test today so we aren't relying on guesswork.
Today? Now? I have to be somewhere by eleven, remember.
The nurse can take it on your way out, it takes about five minutes and you won't need to wait.
Five minutes I can do. Will it hurt?
A small scratch, nothing more.
Fine. Anything I should do in the meantime?
Keep taking the carbimazole exactly the way you have been. And if the fluttering ever comes with a racing heart that won't settle, faintness or chest pain, ring 999 rather than waiting for us.
I wanted to ask about the leaflet that came with the tablets, it says to report sore throats, which seems a bit dramatic.
It's actually quite important with that medicine. A sore throat with a fever should be checked quickly, so do mention it if it ever happens.
Oh. Then I'll remember that too. Anything else I should be afraid of?
Not afraid, just aware. That's the lot from me.
Brilliant. Thank you so much, and sorry again for rushing in late.
You're welcome. Mind the stairs on the way down, the second flight is slippery when it rains.

clinical_assessment.assessment: the thyroid hormone level not being fully settled yet
clinical_assessment.normalized_assessment: Thyroid hormone level not yet stable on treatment

clinical_actions.description: Continue carbimazole unchanged; ring 999 for very fast heart, faintness or chest pain
Report sore throat with fever promptly while on carbimazole

clinical_uncertainties.description: The patient cannot say when the fluttering began.
The patient gives the carbimazole dose tentatively as maybe 20 mg and cannot check the box.
